items.markdown:
A **merchant cash advance (MCA)** is `an alternative financing option where a lender provides an upfront lump sum of cash` . Rather than making fixed monthly repayments, the advance is paid back as a small, pre-agreed percentage of your daily credit and debit card sales.[](https://www.british-business-bank.co.uk/business-guidance/guidance-articles/finance/small-business-guide-to-a-merchant-cash-advance) [[1]](https://www.british-business-bank.co.uk/business-guidance/guidance-articles/finance/small-business-guide-to-a-merchant-cash-advance)[[2]](https://www.money.co.uk/business/business-loans/what-is-a-merchant-cash-advance)[[3]](https://www.merchantsavvy.co.uk/business-finance/merchant-cash-advance/)[[4]](https://www.towerleasing.co.uk/merchant-cash-advance/)

How It Works

- **The Advance:** Lenders typically advance between£3,0 0 0 and£5 0 0,0 0 0 , based on your average monthly card turnover.
- **The Cost:** Instead of an APR, MCAs use a "factor rate" (usually between 1.1 and 1.5). If you take a£1 0,0 0 0 advance with a 1.2 factor rate, your total repayment is£1 2,0 0 0.
- **Repayment:** A set percentage (e.g., 10%) is automatically deducted from every customer card transaction until the£1 2,0 0 0 is cleared.[](https://www.merchantsavvy.co.uk/business-finance/merchant-cash-advance/) [[1]](https://www.merchantsavvy.co.uk/business-finance/merchant-cash-advance/)[[2]](https://www.merchantloanadvance.co.uk/)[[3]](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained)[[4]](https://www.towerleasing.co.uk/merchant-cash-advance/)[[5]](https://www.merchantloanadvance.co.uk/business-types/restaurant-business-loans/)

Pros & Cons

**The Benefits:** 

- **Flexible Repayments:** Payments fluctuate with your sales volume. If you have a slow week, your repayments drop automatically with no penalty.
- **Fast Approval:** Funding can often be accessed in as little as 24-48 hours.
- **No Collateral:** Usually unsecured, meaning you don't need to put up business or personal assets (like property) to secure the funding.
- **Accessible:** Eligibility focuses heavily on your card sales volume rather than just your credit history.[](https://www.british-business-bank.co.uk/business-guidance/guidance-articles/finance/small-business-guide-to-a-merchant-cash-advance) [[1]](https://www.british-business-bank.co.uk/business-guidance/guidance-articles/finance/small-business-guide-to-a-merchant-cash-advance)[[2]](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained)[[3]](https://www.money.co.uk/business/business-loans/what-is-a-merchant-cash-advance)[[4]](https://www.towerleasing.co.uk/merchant-cash-advance/)[[5]](https://www.merchantloanadvance.co.uk/)[[6]](https://www.merchantsavvy.co.uk/business-finance/merchant-cash-advance/)

**The Risks:** 

- **Higher Overall Costs:** The factor rate means MCAs can be a much more expensive form of capital compared to traditional high-street business loans.[](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained) [[1]](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained)[[2]](https://swoopfunding.com/us/business-loans/merchant-cash-advance/what-happens-if-you-default/)
- **Reduced Cash Flow:** Because the percentage is taken off every card sale, it can slightly reduce your daily working capital in real-time.
- **Lack of Early Settlement Benefit:** Because the fee is fixed upfront as a factor rate, paying the advance off early usually does not reduce the total amount of fees you owe.[[1]](https://stripe.com/gb/resources/more/merchant-cash-advance)[[2]](https://www.towerleasing.co.uk/merchant-cash-advance/)

Who Uses It?MCAs are highly popular among businesses with high volumes of point-of-sale (POS) card transactions, such as restaurants, cafes, e-commerce stores, salons, and retail shops.[](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained) [[1]](https://www.iwoca.co.uk/finance-explained/merchant-cash-advance-explained)[[2]](https://www.towerleasing.co.uk/merchant-cash-advance/)Where to Apply If you are considering an MCA, you can compare options through established UK broker and lending networks. You can evaluate lenders and read the full requirements via the [UK Government Business Finance Support](https://www.gov.uk/business-finance-support/merchant-cash-advance-uk) or check out resources provided by the [British Merchant Cash Advance Association (BMCAA)](https://www.bmcaa.co.uk/).[[1]](https://phoenixcf.co.uk/products/business-cash-advance)[[2]](https://www.bmcaa.co.uk/)[[3]](https://www.merchantcashadvance.co.uk/secured-business-loans/)
